```{r}
# ==============================================================
# FINAL CORRECTED PHYSICOCHEMICAL ANALYSIS
#
# DEFINITIVE INPUT:
#   DeQueen.nutrient_metric
#
# IMPORTANT:
#   We use ONLY the source laboratory columns:
#
#     Nitrogen
#     Ammonium.N
#     Phosphorus
#     Potassium
#
#   These are already DRY-BASIS values in lb/US ton.
#
#   Conversion:
#
#     lb/US ton x 0.5 = kg/metric ton
#
#   NO dry-matter correction is applied.
#   DM_frac is NOT used to transform nutrient concentrations.
#
# NEW OBJECTS:
#   Everything created here ends in .final
#
# MODEL STRATEGY:
#
# Global:
#   Level ~ Treatment * Growout + Position + (1 | House)
#
# Growout-specific:
#   Level ~ Treatment + Position + (1 | House)
#
# House is ALWAYS retained.
#
# Distribution:
#   Normal
#   Gamma
#   Log-normal
#
# Distribution is selected independently for:
#   - global model
#   - each growout-specific model
#
# Figure/manuscript within-growout Treatment comparisons:
#   emmeans(~ Treatment | Growout)
#   from GLOBAL model
#
# Baseline:
#   one composite sample per house
#   two-sided Mann-Whitney / Wilcoxon rank-sum test
#
# DHARMa:
#   global models only
# ==============================================================


# ==============================================================
# 0. Packages
# ==============================================================

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(MASS)
library(glmmTMB)
library(car)
library(emmeans)
library(DHARMa)
library(performance)
library(writexl)


# ==============================================================
# 1. REBUILD THE CORRECT METRIC DATA FROM SOURCE COLUMNS
#
# Do NOT trust or use any existing .dry columns.
# ==============================================================

DeQueen.nutrient_metric.final <- DeQueen.nutrient_metric %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Nitrogen.kg_mt =
      as.numeric(Nitrogen) * 0.5,

    Ammonium.N.kg_mt =
      as.numeric(Ammonium.N) * 0.5,

    Phosphorus.kg_mt =
      as.numeric(Phosphorus) * 0.5,

    Potassium.kg_mt =
      as.numeric(Potassium) * 0.5,

    NH4_to_TotalN.final =
      Ammonium.N.kg_mt / Nitrogen.kg_mt
  )


# ==============================================================
# 2. HARD AUDIT OF THE CONVERSION
#
# These checks make it impossible for the old DM-corrected
# values to enter this analysis.
# ==============================================================

nutrient_conversion_audit.final <- DeQueen.nutrient_metric.final %>%
  dplyr::transmute(

    Sample.Name,

    Moisture,

    DM_frac,

    Nitrogen_source =
      as.numeric(Nitrogen),

    Nitrogen_kg_mt =
      Nitrogen.kg_mt,

    Nitrogen_expected =
      as.numeric(Nitrogen) * 0.5,

    NH4_source =
      as.numeric(Ammonium.N),

    NH4_kg_mt =
      Ammonium.N.kg_mt,

    NH4_expected =
      as.numeric(Ammonium.N) * 0.5,

    P_source =
      as.numeric(Phosphorus),

    P_kg_mt =
      Phosphorus.kg_mt,

    P_expected =
      as.numeric(Phosphorus) * 0.5,

    K_source =
      as.numeric(Potassium),

    K_kg_mt =
      Potassium.kg_mt,

    K_expected =
      as.numeric(Potassium) * 0.5
  )


stopifnot(

  all(
    dplyr::near(
      nutrient_conversion_audit.final$Nitrogen_kg_mt,
      nutrient_conversion_audit.final$Nitrogen_expected
    )
  ),

  all(
    dplyr::near(
      nutrient_conversion_audit.final$NH4_kg_mt,
      nutrient_conversion_audit.final$NH4_expected
    )
  ),

  all(
    dplyr::near(
      nutrient_conversion_audit.final$P_kg_mt,
      nutrient_conversion_audit.final$P_expected
    )
  ),

  all(
    dplyr::near(
      nutrient_conversion_audit.final$K_kg_mt,
      nutrient_conversion_audit.final$K_expected
    )
  )
)


cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "CONVERSION AUDIT PASSED\n",
  "Source dry-basis lb/US ton -> kg/metric ton x 0.5\n",
  "NO DM_frac correction applied\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)


print(
  nutrient_conversion_audit.final %>%
    dplyr::select(
      Sample.Name,
      Moisture,
      DM_frac,
      Nitrogen_source,
      Nitrogen_kg_mt,
      NH4_source,
      NH4_kg_mt,
      P_source,
      P_kg_mt,
      K_source,
      K_kg_mt
    ) %>%
    utils::head(10)
)


# ==============================================================
# 3. BUILD FRESH LONG-FORMAT DATA
# ==============================================================

Nutrient_long.metric.final <- DeQueen.nutrient_metric.final %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(

    cols = dplyr::all_of(
      c(
        "Ammonium.N.kg_mt",
        "Nitrogen.kg_mt",
        "Phosphorus.kg_mt",
        "Potassium.kg_mt",
        "Moisture",
        "NH4_to_TotalN.final"
      )
    ),

    names_to =
      "Metric",

    values_to =
      "Level"
  ) %>%

  dplyr::mutate(

    Growout =
      factor(
        as.character(Growout),
        levels = c(
          "Baseline",
          "1",
          "2"
        )
      ),

    Treatment =
      factor(
        as.character(Treatment),
        levels = c(
          "Control",
          "IndigoLT"
        )
      ),

    Position =
      factor(
        as.character(Position)
      ),

    House =
      factor(
        as.character(House)
      ),

    Metric =
      dplyr::recode(

        Metric,

        "Ammonium.N.kg_mt" =
          "NH4+ (kg/mt)",

        "Nitrogen.kg_mt" =
          "Total N (kg/mt)",

        "Phosphorus.kg_mt" =
          "P (kg/mt)",

        "Potassium.kg_mt" =
          "K (kg/mt)",

        "Moisture" =
          "Moisture (% wb)",

        "NH4_to_TotalN.final" =
          "NH4+/Total N"
      ),

    Metric =
      factor(
        Metric,
        levels = c(
          "NH4+ (kg/mt)",
          "Total N (kg/mt)",
          "NH4+/Total N",
          "P (kg/mt)",
          "K (kg/mt)",
          "Moisture (% wb)"
        )
      )
  ) %>%

  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(Level),
    !is.na(Growout),
    !is.na(Treatment)
  )


# ==============================================================
# 4. SECOND AUDIT:
# CONFIRM LONG-FORMAT VALUES ARE THE CORRECT ONES
# ==============================================================

nutrient_long_audit.final <- Nutrient_long.metric.final %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    as.character(Metric) %in% c(
      "NH4+ (kg/mt)",
      "Total N (kg/mt)",
      "P (kg/mt)",
      "K (kg/mt)"
    )
  ) %>%

  dplyr::mutate(

    Expected.final =
      dplyr::case_when(

        as.character(Metric) ==
          "NH4+ (kg/mt)" ~
          as.numeric(Ammonium.N) * 0.5,

        as.character(Metric) ==
          "Total N (kg/mt)" ~
          as.numeric(Nitrogen) * 0.5,

        as.character(Metric) ==
          "P (kg/mt)" ~
          as.numeric(Phosphorus) * 0.5,

        as.character(Metric) ==
          "K (kg/mt)" ~
          as.numeric(Potassium) * 0.5,

        TRUE ~
          NA_real_
      ),

    Difference.final =
      Level - Expected.final
  )


stopifnot(
  max(
    abs(
      nutrient_long_audit.final$Difference.final
    ),
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) < 1e-10
)


cat(
  "\nLong-format audit passed.\n"
)


# ==============================================================
# 5. BASELINE TESTS
#
# One composite sample per house.
#
# Uses the SAME two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum settings as the
# original workflow:
#   exact = FALSE
#   correct = FALSE
# ==============================================================

rbc_two_sample.metric.final <- function(x, y) {
  diffs <- outer(y, x, FUN = "-")
  mean(sign(diffs))
}


wilcox_baseline.metric.final <- Nutrient_long.metric.final %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Growout == "Baseline"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    Metric
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ {

    df_baseline.final <- .x

    trts.final <- unique(
      df_baseline.final$Treatment
    )


    if (
      length(trts.final) != 2
    ) {

      return(
        tibble::tibble(
          Analysis =
            "Baseline",

          Growout =
            "Baseline",

          Family =
            NA_character_,

          Transform =
            "none",

          N =
            nrow(
              df_baseline.final
            ),

          Result_type =
            "Wilcoxon rank-sum",

          Effect_or_contrast =
            NA_character_,

          Estimate =
            NA_real_,

          SE =
            NA_real_,

          df =
            NA_real_,

          Test_statistic =
            NA_real_,

          P_value =
            NA_real_,

          Variance =
            NA_real_,

          SD =
            NA_real_,

          ICC_adjusted =
            NA_real_,

          ICC_unadjusted =
            NA_real_,

          Percent_House_adjusted =
            NA_real_,

          Percent_House_unadjusted =
            NA_real_
        )
      )
    }


    if (
      all(
        c(
          "Control",
          "IndigoLT"
        ) %in%
          as.character(
            trts.final
          )
      )
    ) {

      g1.final <- "Control"
      g2.final <- "IndigoLT"

    } else {

      ord.final <- sort(
        as.character(
          trts.final
        )
      )

      g1.final <- ord.final[1]
      g2.final <- ord.final[2]
    }


    x.final <- df_baseline.final$Level[
      df_baseline.final$Treatment ==
        g1.final
    ]

    y.final <- df_baseline.final$Level[
      df_baseline.final$Treatment ==
        g2.final
    ]


    wilcox_fit.final <- suppressWarnings(
      stats::wilcox.test(
        x.final,
        y.final,
        alternative =
          "two.sided",
        exact =
          FALSE,
        correct =
          FALSE
      )
    )


    rank_biserial.final <-
      rbc_two_sample.metric.final(
        x.final,
        y.final
      )


    tibble::tibble(
      Analysis =
        "Baseline",

      Growout =
        "Baseline",

      Family =
        NA_character_,

      Transform =
        "none",

      N =
        length(x.final) +
        length(y.final),

      Result_type =
        "Wilcoxon rank-sum",

      Effect_or_contrast =
        paste0(
          g2.final,
          " - ",
          g1.final
        ),

      Estimate =
        rank_biserial.final,

      SE =
        NA_real_,

      df =
        NA_real_,

      Test_statistic =
        as.numeric(
          wilcox_fit.final$statistic
        ),

      P_value =
        unname(
          wilcox_fit.final$p.value
        ),

      Variance =
        NA_real_,

      SD =
        NA_real_,

      ICC_adjusted =
        NA_real_,

      ICC_unadjusted =
        NA_real_,

      Percent_House_adjusted =
        NA_real_,

      Percent_House_unadjusted =
        NA_real_
    )
  }) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()


cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "BASELINE TESTS\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)


print(
  wilcox_baseline.metric.final %>%
    dplyr::select(
      Metric,
      Result_type,
      Test_statistic,
      Estimate,
      P_value
    ),
  n = Inf
)


# ==============================================================
# 6. DISTRIBUTION-SELECTION HELPER
# ==============================================================

fit_dists_AIC.metric.final <- function(
  y
) {

  y <- y[
    is.finite(y)
  ]


  fits.final <- list()


  fits.final$normal <- tryCatch(

    MASS::fitdistr(
      y,
      "normal"
    ),

    error =
      function(e) NULL
  )


  y_positive.final <- y[
    y > 0
  ]


  fits.final$gamma <- if (
    length(
      y_positive.final
    ) > 1
  ) {

    tryCatch(

      MASS::fitdistr(
        y_positive.final,
        "gamma"
      ),

      error =
        function(e) NULL
    )

  } else {

    NULL
  }


  fits.final$lognorm <- if (
    length(
      y_positive.final
    ) > 1
  ) {

    tryCatch(

      MASS::fitdistr(
        y_positive.final,
        "lognormal"
      ),

      error =
        function(e) NULL
    )

  } else {

    NULL
  }


  aics.final <- c(

    normal =
      if (
        !is.null(
          fits.final$normal
        )
      ) {
        AIC(
          fits.final$normal
        )
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },

    gamma =
      if (
        !is.null(
          fits.final$gamma
        )
      ) {
        AIC(
          fits.final$gamma
        )
      } else {
        NA_real_
      },

    lognorm =
      if (
        !is.null(
          fits.final$lognorm
        )
      ) {
        AIC(
          fits.final$lognorm
        )
      } else {
        NA_real_
      }
  )


  valid_aics.final <- aics.final[
    is.finite(
      aics.final
    )
  ]


  if (
    length(
      valid_aics.final
    ) == 0
  ) {

    stop(
      "No candidate distribution could be fitted."
    )
  }


  best.final <- names(
    which.min(
      valid_aics.final
    )
  )[1]


  list(

    AICs =
      aics.final,

    Best =
      best.final
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 7. FAMILY HELPER
# ==============================================================

get_family.metric.final <- function(
  family_name
) {

  if (
    family_name == "normal"
  ) {

    return(
      gaussian(
        link = "identity"
      )
    )
  }


  if (
    family_name == "gamma"
  ) {

    return(
      Gamma(
        link = "log"
      )
    )
  }


  if (
    family_name == "lognorm"
  ) {

    return(
      gaussian(
        link = "identity"
      )
    )
  }


  stop(
    "Unsupported family: ",
    family_name
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 8. MODEL-FITTING HELPER
#
# House is ALWAYS retained.
# ==============================================================

fit_model.metric.final <- function(
  data,
  family_name,
  scope = c(
    "global",
    "growout"
  )
) {

  scope <- match.arg(
    scope
  )


  data.final <- data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(

      Treatment =
        factor(
          as.character(Treatment),
          levels = c(
            "Control",
            "IndigoLT"
          )
        ),

      Growout =
        factor(
          as.character(Growout)
        ),

      Position =
        factor(
          as.character(Position)
        ),

      House =
        factor(
          as.character(House)
        )
    ) %>%
    droplevels()


  response.final <-
    "Level"


  if (
    family_name ==
      "lognorm"
  ) {

    if (
      any(
        data.final$Level <= 0,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    ) {

      stop(
        "Non-positive value encountered in log-normal model."
      )
    }


    data.final$Level_log.final <-
      log(
        data.final$Level
      )


    response.final <-
      "Level_log.final"
  }


  if (
    scope ==
      "global"
  ) {

    formula.final <- stats::as.formula(
      paste0(
        response.final,
        " ~ Treatment * Growout + Position + (1 | House)"
      )
    )

  } else {

    formula.final <- stats::as.formula(
      paste0(
        response.final,
        " ~ Treatment + Position + (1 | House)"
      )
    )
  }


  glmmTMB::glmmTMB(

    formula.final,

    family =
      get_family.metric.final(
        family_name
      ),

    data =
      data.final
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 9. HOUSE VARIANCE + ICC HELPER
# ==============================================================

get_house_stats.metric.final <- function(
  model,
  family_name
) {

  variance_components.final <-
    glmmTMB::VarCorr(
      model
    )$cond


  house_variance.final <-
    as.numeric(
      variance_components.final$House[
        1,
        1
      ]
    )


  house_sd.final <-
    sqrt(
      house_variance.final
    )


  if (
    family_name ==
      "gamma"
  ) {

    icc.final <- suppressWarnings(
      tryCatch(

        performance::icc(
          model,
          tolerance = 0,
          approximation = "lognormal"
        ),

        error =
          function(e) NULL
      )
    )

  } else {

    icc.final <- suppressWarnings(
      tryCatch(

        performance::icc(
          model,
          tolerance = 0
        ),

        error =
          function(e) NULL
      )
    )
  }


  if (
    is.null(
      icc.final
    )
  ) {

    icc_adjusted.final <-
      NA_real_

    icc_unadjusted.final <-
      NA_real_

  } else {

    icc_adjusted.final <-
      as.numeric(
        icc.final$ICC_adjusted
      )[1]

    icc_unadjusted.final <-
      as.numeric(
        icc.final$ICC_unadjusted
      )[1]
  }


  data.frame(

    Variance =
      house_variance.final,

    SD =
      house_sd.final,

    ICC_adjusted =
      icc_adjusted.final,

    ICC_unadjusted =
      icc_unadjusted.final,

    Percent_House_adjusted =
      icc_adjusted.final * 100,

    Percent_House_unadjusted =
      icc_unadjusted.final * 100
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 10. EMMEANS STATISTIC HELPER
# ==============================================================

get_emmeans_stat.metric.final <- function(
  data
) {

  if (
    "z.ratio" %in%
      names(data)
  ) {

    return(
      as.numeric(
        data$z.ratio
      )
    )
  }


  if (
    "t.ratio" %in%
      names(data)
  ) {

    return(
      as.numeric(
        data$t.ratio
      )
    )
  }


  rep(
    NA_real_,
    nrow(data)
  )
}


# ==============================================================
# 11. DATA USED FOR GLMMs
#
# Growouts 1 and 2 only.
# ==============================================================

Nutrient_model_data.metric.final <- Nutrient_long.metric.final %>%
  dplyr::filter(

    as.character(Growout) %in%
      c(
        "1",
        "2"
      ),

    !is.na(Position),

    !is.na(House)
  ) %>%
  droplevels()


# ==============================================================
# 12. SUM-TO-ZERO CONTRASTS FOR TYPE III TESTS
# ==============================================================

old_contrasts.metric.final <- options(
  contrasts = c(
    "contr.sum",
    "contr.poly"
  )
)


# ==============================================================
# 13. GLOBAL DISTRIBUTION SELECTION
# ==============================================================

metrics.metric.final <- levels(
  droplevels(
    Nutrient_model_data.metric.final$Metric
  )
)


distribution_rows.metric.final <- list()


for (
  metric_name.final in
  metrics.metric.final
) {

  metric_data.final <- Nutrient_model_data.metric.final %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      as.character(Metric) ==
        metric_name.final
    )


  dist_result.final <-
    fit_dists_AIC.metric.final(
      metric_data.final$Level
    )


  distribution_rows.metric.final[
    metric_name.final
  ] <- list(

    data.frame(

      Analysis =
        "Global",

      Metric =
        metric_name.final,

      Growout =
        "All",

      Normal_AIC =
        as.numeric(
          dist_result.final$AICs["normal"]
        ),

      Gamma_AIC =
        as.numeric(
          dist_result.final$AICs["gamma"]
        ),

      Lognormal_AIC =
        as.numeric(
          dist_result.final$AICs["lognorm"]
        ),

      Selected_family =
        dist_result.final$Best,

      stringsAsFactors =
        FALSE
    )
  )
}


nutrient_distribution_summary.metric.final <-
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    distribution_rows.metric.final
  )


cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "GLOBAL DISTRIBUTION SELECTION\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)


print(
  nutrient_distribution_summary.metric.final,
  n = Inf
)


# ==============================================================
# 14. FIT ALL GLOBAL + GROWOUT-SPECIFIC MODELS
# ==============================================================

nutrient_models.metric.final <- list()

growout_distribution_rows.metric.final <- list()


for (
  metric_name.final in
  metrics.metric.final
) {

  cat(
    "\n============================================================\n",
    metric_name.final,
    "\n============================================================\n",
    sep = ""
  )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Global data
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  metric_data.final <- Nutrient_model_data.metric.final %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      as.character(Metric) ==
        metric_name.final
    ) %>%
    droplevels()


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Global distribution
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  global_dist.final <-
    fit_dists_AIC.metric.final(
      metric_data.final$Level
    )


  global_family.final <-
    global_dist.final$Best


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Global model
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  global_model.final <-
    fit_model.metric.final(

      data =
        metric_data.final,

      family_name =
        global_family.final,

      scope =
        "global"
    )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Global Type III
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  global_anova.final <-
    car::Anova(
      global_model.final,
      type = 3
    )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Global-model emmeans:
  # Treatment within each Growout
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  global_emmeans.final <-
    emmeans::emmeans(
      global_model.final,
      ~ Treatment | Growout
    )


  global_pairs.final <-
    emmeans::contrast(
      global_emmeans.final,
      method = "pairwise",
      adjust = "BH"
    )


  global_pairs_df.final <-
    as.data.frame(
      summary(
        global_pairs.final,
        infer = c(
          TRUE,
          TRUE
        )
      )
    )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Global House variance / ICC
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  global_house.final <-
    get_house_stats.metric.final(
      global_model.final,
      global_family.final
    )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Global DHARMa
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  global_dharma.final <-
    DHARMa::simulateResiduals(
      fittedModel =
        global_model.final,
      n =
        1000
    )


  global_dispersion.final <-
    DHARMa::testDispersion(
      global_dharma.final
    )


  global_outliers.final <-
    DHARMa::testOutliers(
      global_dharma.final
    )


  global_quantiles.final <-
    DHARMa::testQuantiles(
      global_dharma.final
    )


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Growout-specific models
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  pergo_models.final <- list()


  for (
    growout_name.final in
    c(
      "1",
      "2"
    )
  ) {

    growout_data.final <- metric_data.final %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        as.character(Growout) ==
          growout_name.final
      ) %>%
      droplevels()


    growout_dist.final <-
      fit_dists_AIC.metric.final(
        growout_data.final$Level
      )


    growout_family.final <-
      growout_dist.final$Best


    growout_model.final <-
      fit_model.metric.final(

        data =
          growout_data.final,

        family_name =
          growout_family.final,

        scope =
          "growout"
      )


    growout_anova.final <-
      car::Anova(
        growout_model.final,
        type = 3
      )


    growout_house.final <-
      get_house_stats.metric.final(
        growout_model.final,
        growout_family.final
      )


    pergo_models.final[
      growout_name.final
    ] <- list(

      list(

        Growout =
          growout_name.final,

        Family =
          growout_family.final,

        Transform =
          if (
            growout_family.final ==
              "lognorm"
          ) {
            "log"
          } else {
            "none"
          },

        N =
          stats::nobs(
            growout_model.final
          ),

        Model =
          growout_model.final,

        Anova =
          growout_anova.final,

        House =
          growout_house.final
      )
    )


    growout_distribution_rows.metric.final[
      paste(
        metric_name.final,
        growout_name.final,
        sep = "_"
      )
    ] <- list(

      data.frame(

        Analysis =
          "Growout-specific",

        Metric =
          metric_name.final,

        Growout =
          growout_name.final,

        Normal_AIC =
          as.numeric(
            growout_dist.final$AICs["normal"]
          ),

        Gamma_AIC =
          as.numeric(
            growout_dist.final$AICs["gamma"]
          ),

        Lognormal_AIC =
          as.numeric(
            growout_dist.final$AICs["lognorm"]
          ),

        Selected_family =
          growout_family.final,

        stringsAsFactors =
          FALSE
      )
    )
  }


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Save complete metric result
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  nutrient_models.metric.final[
    metric_name.final
  ] <- list(

    list(

      Metric =
        metric_name.final,

      Family =
        global_family.final,

      Transform =
        if (
          global_family.final ==
            "lognorm"
        ) {
          "log"
        } else {
          "none"
        },

      N =
        stats::nobs(
          global_model.final
        ),

      Model =
        global_model.final,

      Anova =
        global_anova.final,

      Emmeans =
        global_emmeans.final,

      Pairs =
        global_pairs.final,

      Pairs_df =
        global_pairs_df.final,

      House =
        global_house.final,

      DHARMa_sim =
        global_dharma.final,

      DHARMa_dispersion =
        global_dispersion.final,

      DHARMa_outliers =
        global_outliers.final,

      DHARMa_quantiles =
        global_quantiles.final,

      Growout_models =
        pergo_models.final
    )
  )
}

# 15. COMPLETE DISTRIBUTION TABLE

nutrient_result_rows.metric.final <- list()


for (

) {

  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
```

```{r}
##Visualization (METRIC) — MATCH TEMPLATE AESTHETICS EXACTLY
## Uses:
##   - Nutrient_long.metric.final
##   - nutrient_glmm_results.metric.final
##   - predefined pal_fill, pal_color, dodge_width
##
## Corrected nutrient values:
##   source dry-basis lb/US ton × 0.5 = kg/metric ton
##
## Statistics:
##   - Baseline = Mann-Whitney / Wilcoxon
##   - Growout 1 and 2 = global House-retained GLMM
##     Treatment contrasts within Growout
##
## Reuses existing .house_icc plotting object names


## =====================================================================
## 1) Format p-values
##
## p >= 0.001:
##   0.032
##
## p < 0.001:
##   3.86e-4
## =====================================================================

format_p_metric.house_icc <- function(p) {

  if (is.na(p)) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }

  if (p < 0.001) {

    x <- formatC(
      p,
      format = "e",
      digits = 2
    )

    # Remove unnecessary trailing zeros
    x <- sub(
      "0+e",
      "e",
      x
    )

    x <- sub(
      "\\.e",
      "e",
      x
    )

    # Simplify exponent:
    # e-04 -> e-4
    # e+03 -> e3
    x <- sub(
      "e-0+",
      "e-",
      x
    )

    x <- sub(
      "e\\+0*",
      "e",
      x
    )

    return(
      paste0(
        "italic(p) == '",
        x,
        "'"
      )
    )
  }

  sprintf(
    "italic(p) == %.3f",
    p
  )
}


## =====================================================================
## 2) Build p-value labels for plotting from corrected final stats object
## =====================================================================

p_values_plot_df.metric.house_icc <- nutrient_glmm_results.metric.final %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Analysis == "Baseline" |
      (
        Analysis == "Within-growout" &
          Result_type == "Treatment contrast - emmeans"
      )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Metric, Growout) %>%
  dplyr::slice(1) %>%  # ensure single row per Metric × Growout
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Metric  = factor(
      Metric,
      levels = levels(Nutrient_long.metric.final$Metric)
    ),
    Growout = factor(
      Growout,
      levels = levels(Nutrient_long.metric.final$Growout)
    ),
    P_Value = P_value,
    P_Label = vapply(
      P_Value,
      format_p_metric.house_icc,
      character(1)
    )
  )


## =====================================================================
## 3) y-positions just above the tallest point per Metric × Growout
## =====================================================================

y_pos_df.metric.house_icc <- Nutrient_long.metric.final %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Metric, Growout) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    y_pos = max(Level, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.03,
    .groups = "drop"
  )


p_values_plot_df.metric.house_icc <- dplyr::left_join(
  p_values_plot_df.metric.house_icc,
  y_pos_df.metric.house_icc,
  by = c("Metric", "Growout")
)


## =====================================================================
## 4) Helper data for plot: stripe + mean lines
## =====================================================================

g_levels.metric.house_icc <- levels(
  Nutrient_long.metric.final$Growout
)

idx1.metric.house_icc <- which(
  g_levels.metric.house_icc == "1"
)


stripes_df.metric.house_icc <- tibble::tibble(
  xmin = if (length(idx1.metric.house_icc))
    idx1.metric.house_icc - 0.5
  else
    NA_real_,
  xmax = if (length(idx1.metric.house_icc))
    idx1.metric.house_icc + 0.5
  else
    NA_real_
) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    is.finite(xmin),
    is.finite(xmax)
  )


mean_levels_df.metric.house_icc <- Nutrient_long.metric.final %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Metric, Growout, Treatment) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Mean_Level = mean(Level, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


## =====================================================================
## 5) Graphics params — SAME AS ORIGINAL
## =====================================================================

if (!exists("dodge_width"))
  dodge_width <- 0.6


if (!exists("pal_fill")) {

  trts <- levels(
    Nutrient_long.metric.final$Treatment
  )

  pal_fill <- stats::setNames(
    RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(
      max(3, length(trts)),
      "Set2"
    )[seq_along(trts)],
    trts
  )
}


if (!exists("pal_color"))
  pal_color <- pal_fill


## =====================================================================
## 6) Plot — COPY ORIGINAL TEMPLATE AESTHETICS EXACTLY
## =====================================================================

p.metric.horizontal.house_icc <- ggplot(
  Nutrient_long.metric.final,
  aes(
    x = Growout,
    y = Level
  )
) +

  # Light stripe for Growout "1"
  {
    if (nrow(stripes_df.metric.house_icc))

      geom_rect(

    )
  ) +

  # Mean points
  stat_summary(
    aes(fill = Treatment),
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    shape = 23,

    color = "white",

      width = dodge_width

  # Jittered observations
  geom_jitter(
    aes(color = Treatment),

  # Treatment trendlines (means)
  geom_line(
```

```{r}
# ================================================================
# MICROBIOME COMPOSITION vs. PHYSICOCHEMICAL VARIABLES
# REVISED HOUSE-RESTRICTED PERMUTATION ANALYSIS
#
# Includes:
#   1) PERMANOVA
#   2) PROTEST
#   3) Mantel tests
#   4) db-RDA
#
# Experimental structure:
#   - Treatment assigned at House level
#   - Growout repeated within House
#   - Positions A-E are recurring physical locations within House
#   - The same Position is retained across Growouts
#
# Permutation structure used here:
#   - permutations occur within House
#   - each House x Position trajectory is moved as an intact unit
#   - the Growout 1 and Growout 2 observations for a Position
#     therefore remain linked
#
# IMPORTANT:
#   The PERMANOVA model includes Treatment, Growout, Position,
#   and Treatment:Growout as adjustment variables.
#
#   The permutation scheme below is designed for inference on the
#   sample-level physicochemical variables. Therefore, ONLY the
#   physicochemical-variable rows are extracted/interpreted from
#   these PERMANOVA fits.
#
#   Treatment, Growout, Position, and Treatment:Growout inference
#   should come from the dedicated beta-diversity analysis with the
#   factor-specific permutation schemes.
#
#   The db-RDA retains the ORIGINAL model structure:
#     focal environmental variable +
#     Condition(House + Growout + Treatment + Position)
#
#   Other physicochemical variables are NOT included in the
#   Condition() term.
#
# Does NOT overwrite previous .metric objects.
# ================================================================


library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(vegan)
library(permute)
library(phyloseq)


# ================================================================
# 0. Settings
# ================================================================

n_permutations.metric_houseperm <- 9999L

env_vars.metric_houseperm <- c(
  "Nitrogen.dry",
  "Ammonium.N.dry",
  "Phosphorus.dry",
  "Potassium.dry",
  "Moisture"
)


# ================================================================
# 1. Extract metadata
# ================================================================

sample_data_df.metric_houseperm <- data.frame(
  phyloseq::sample_data(
    physeq_no_growout3_css_nutr.metric
  )
)


sample_data_df.metric_houseperm$Position <- factor(
  sample_data_df.metric_houseperm$Position
)

sample_data_df.metric_houseperm$House <- factor(
  sample_data_df.metric_houseperm$House
)

sample_data_df.metric_houseperm$Growout <- factor(
  sample_data_df.metric_houseperm$Growout
)

sample_data_df.metric_houseperm$Treatment <- factor(
  sample_data_df.metric_houseperm$Treatment
)


# ================================================================
# 2. Confirm required columns
# ================================================================

required_vars.metric_houseperm <- c(
  "Treatment",
  "House",
  "Growout",
  "Position",
  env_vars.metric_houseperm
)


missing_vars.metric_houseperm <- setdiff(
  required_vars.metric_houseperm,
  colnames(
    sample_data_df.metric_houseperm
  )
)


if (
  length(
    missing_vars.metric_houseperm
  ) > 0
) {

  stop(
    paste(
      "Missing required metadata columns:",
      paste(
        missing_vars.metric_houseperm,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}


# ================================================================
# 3. Retain complete cases for the full environmental model
# ================================================================

complete_rows.metric_houseperm <- stats::complete.cases(
  sample_data_df.metric_houseperm[
    ,
    required_vars.metric_houseperm,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
)


analysis_ids.metric_houseperm <- rownames(
  sample_data_df.metric_houseperm
)[
  complete_rows.metric_houseperm
]


if (
  length(
    analysis_ids.metric_houseperm
  ) < 10
) {

  stop(
    "Too few complete samples for the environmental composition analysis."
  )
}


if (
  sum(
    !complete_rows.metric_houseperm
  ) > 0
) {

  message(
    "Dropping ",
    sum(
      !complete_rows.metric_houseperm
    ),
    " samples with incomplete environmental/design metadata."
  )
}


sample_data_df.metric_houseperm <-
  sample_data_df.metric_houseperm[
    analysis_ids.metric_houseperm,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]


sample_data_df.metric_houseperm <- droplevels(
  sample_data_df.metric_houseperm
)


# ================================================================
# 4. Build community distance matrices
# ================================================================

bray_dist_full.metric_houseperm <- phyloseq::distance(
  physeq_no_growout3_css_nutr.metric,
  method = "bray"
)


wunifrac_dist_full.metric_houseperm <- phyloseq::UniFrac(
  physeq_no_growout3_css_nutr.metric,
  weighted = TRUE,
  normalized = TRUE,
  parallel = FALSE
)


uunifrac_dist_full.metric_houseperm <- phyloseq::UniFrac(
  physeq_no_growout3_css_nutr.metric,
  weighted = FALSE,
  normalized = TRUE,
  parallel = FALSE
)


# ================================================================
# 5. Helper: subset/reorder distance matrix to analysis IDs
# ================================================================

subset_dist.metric_houseperm <- function(
  distance_object_houseperm,
  keep_ids_houseperm
) {

  distance_matrix_houseperm <- as.matrix(
    distance_object_houseperm
  )


  if (
    !all(
      keep_ids_houseperm %in%
        rownames(
          distance_matrix_houseperm
        )
    )
  ) {

    stop(
      "Not all analysis sample IDs were found in the distance matrix."
    )
  }


  stats::as.dist(
    distance_matrix_houseperm[
      keep_ids_houseperm,
      keep_ids_houseperm,
      drop = FALSE
    ]
  )
}


bray_dist.metric_houseperm <- subset_dist.metric_houseperm(
  bray_dist_full.metric_houseperm,
  analysis_ids.metric_houseperm
)


wunifrac_dist.metric_houseperm <- subset_dist.metric_houseperm(
  wunifrac_dist_full.metric_houseperm,
  analysis_ids.metric_houseperm
)


uunifrac_dist.metric_houseperm <- subset_dist.metric_houseperm(
  uunifrac_dist_full.metric_houseperm,
  analysis_ids.metric_houseperm
)


# ================================================================
# 6. Define recurring House x Position units
#
# Each House x Position unit contains the same physical location
# sampled in Growout 1 and Growout 2.
# ================================================================

sample_data_df.metric_houseperm$House_Position_houseperm <-
  interaction(
    sample_data_df.metric_houseperm$House,
    sample_data_df.metric_houseperm$Position,
    drop = TRUE,
    sep = ":"
  )


house_position_counts.metric_houseperm <- table(
  sample_data_df.metric_houseperm$House_Position_houseperm
)


cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "HOUSE x POSITION SAMPLE COUNTS\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)


print(
  house_position_counts.metric_houseperm
)


# With two microbiome growouts, each recurring physical Position
# should have two observations.

if (
  any(
    house_position_counts.metric_houseperm != 2
  )
) {

  stop(
    paste(
      "At least one House x Position unit does not contain exactly",
      "two observations. Check missing samples before constructing",
      "the linked-position permutation design."
    )
  )
}


# Confirm that each House x Position contains both Growouts

house_position_growout.metric_houseperm <- with(
  sample_data_df.metric_houseperm,
  table(
    House_Position_houseperm,
    Growout
  )
)


if (
  any(
    house_position_growout.metric_houseperm != 1
  )
) {

  stop(
    paste(
      "Each House x Position unit should contain exactly one",
      "observation from each Growout."
    )
  )
}


# ================================================================
# 7. Build restricted environmental permutation matrix
#
# House = permutation block
#
# House x Position = whole plot
#
# within = none
#
# Therefore:
#   - samples never move between Houses
#   - Position trajectories can exchange within House
#   - G1 and G2 observations for the same physical Position
#     remain together
# ================================================================

set.seed(1)


perm_control_env.metric_houseperm <- permute::how(

  nperm =
    n_permutations.metric_houseperm,

  blocks =
    sample_data_df.metric_houseperm$House,

  plots =
    permute::Plots(
      strata =
        sample_data_df.metric_houseperm$House_Position_houseperm,
      type =
        "free"
    ),

  within =
    permute::Within(
      type =
        "none"
    ),

  complete =
    FALSE
)


perm_env.metric_houseperm <- permute::shuffleSet(

  n =
    nrow(
      sample_data_df.metric_houseperm
    ),

  nset =
    n_permutations.metric_houseperm,

  control =
    perm_control_env.metric_houseperm
)


cat(
  "\nRestricted environmental permutations generated:",
  nrow(
    perm_env.metric_houseperm
  ),
  "\n"
)


# ================================================================
# 8. PERMANOVA
#
# Model:
#
#   distance ~ Treatment * Growout + Position +
#              NH4 + Total N + P + K + Moisture
#
# Treatment, Growout, Position, and Treatment:Growout are included
# as adjustment variables.
#
# Only environmental-variable rows are interpreted from these fits.
#
# by = "margin" gives the contribution of each environmental
# variable while accounting for the other terms in the model.
# ================================================================

form_metric_env_houseperm <- ~
  Treatment * Growout +
  Position +
  Ammonium.N.dry +
  Nitrogen.dry +
  Phosphorus.dry +
  Potassium.dry +
  Moisture


permanova_bray_env.metric_houseperm <- vegan::adonis2(

  update(
    form_metric_env_houseperm,
    bray_dist.metric_houseperm ~ .
  ),

  data =
    sample_data_df.metric_houseperm,

  permutations =
    perm_env.metric_houseperm,

  by =
    "margin"
)


permanova_wunifrac_env.metric_houseperm <- vegan::adonis2(

  update(
    form_metric_env_houseperm,
    wunifrac_dist.metric_houseperm ~ .
  ),

  data =
    sample_data_df.metric_houseperm,

  permutations =
    perm_env.metric_houseperm,

  by =
    "margin"
)


permanova_uunifrac_env.metric_houseperm <- vegan::adonis2(

  update(
    form_metric_env_houseperm,
    uunifrac_dist.metric_houseperm ~ .
  ),

  data =
    sample_data_df.metric_houseperm,

  permutations =
    perm_env.metric_houseperm,

  by =
    "margin"
)


# ================================================================
# 9. Extract environmental PERMANOVA terms only
#
# Do NOT use the design-factor p-values from the above models.
# ================================================================

extract_permanova_env.metric_houseperm <- function(
  ad2_obj_houseperm,
  metric_label_houseperm,
  env_vars_houseperm
) {

  df_houseperm <- as.data.frame(
    ad2_obj_houseperm,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )


  df_houseperm$Variable <- rownames(
    df_houseperm
  )


  df_houseperm <- df_houseperm[
    df_houseperm$Variable %in%
      env_vars_houseperm,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]


  if (
    nrow(
      df_houseperm
    ) == 0
  ) {

    return(
      NULL
    )
  }


  pcol_houseperm <- grep(
    "^Pr\\(>F\\)$",
    names(
      df_houseperm
    ),
    value = TRUE
  )


  if (
    length(
      pcol_houseperm
    ) != 1
  ) {

    stop(
      "Could not identify the PERMANOVA p-value column."
    )
  }


  out_houseperm <- data.frame(

    Variable =
      df_houseperm$Variable,

    Effect =
      as.numeric(
        df_houseperm[
          ,
          "R2",
          drop = TRUE
        ]
      ),

    p_value =
      as.numeric(
        df_houseperm[
          ,
          pcol_houseperm,
          drop = TRUE
        ]
      ),

    Metric =
      metric_label_houseperm,

    Analysis =
      "PERMANOVA (margin)",

    Stat =
      "partial R2",

    stringsAsFactors =
      FALSE,

    check.names =
      FALSE
  )


  out_houseperm$q_value <- stats::p.adjust(
    out_houseperm$p_value,
    method = "BH"
  )


  out_houseperm
}


perm_env_bray.metric_houseperm <-
  extract_permanova_env.metric_houseperm(

    permanova_bray_env.metric_houseperm,

    "Bray-Curtis",

    env_vars.metric_houseperm
  )


perm_env_wunifrac.metric_houseperm <-
  extract_permanova_env.metric_houseperm(

    permanova_wunifrac_env.metric_houseperm,

    "Weighted UniFrac",

    env_vars.metric_houseperm
  )


perm_env_uunifrac.metric_houseperm <-
  extract_permanova_env.metric_houseperm(

    permanova_uunifrac_env.metric_houseperm,

    "Unweighted UniFrac",

    env_vars.metric_houseperm
  )


perm_env_long.metric_houseperm <- dplyr::bind_rows(

  perm_env_bray.metric_houseperm,
  perm_env_wunifrac.metric_houseperm,
  perm_env_uunifrac.metric_houseperm
)


cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "ENVIRONMENTAL PERMANOVA RESULTS\n",
  "HOUSE-RESTRICTED PERMUTATIONS\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)


print(
  perm_env_long.metric_houseperm %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Effect =
        round(
          Effect,
          4
        ),
      p_value =
        signif(
          p_value,
          4
        ),
      q_value =
        signif(
          q_value,
          4
        )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      Metric,
      Variable
    ),
  n = Inf
)


# ================================================================
# 10. Standardized environmental matrix for PROTEST and Mantel
# ================================================================

env_raw.metric_houseperm <-
  sample_data_df.metric_houseperm[
    ,
    env_vars.metric_houseperm,
    drop = FALSE
  ]


env_std.metric_houseperm <- scale(
  env_raw.metric_houseperm
)


rownames(
  env_std.metric_houseperm
) <- rownames(
  sample_data_df.metric_houseperm
)


env_dist.metric_houseperm <- vegan::vegdist(
  env_std.metric_houseperm,
  method = "euclidean"
)


cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "ENVIRONMENTAL MATRIX\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)


cat(
  "Variables:",
  paste(
    colnames(
      env_std.metric_houseperm
    ),
    collapse = ", "
  ),
  "\n"
)


cat(
  "Samples:",
  nrow(
    env_std.metric_houseperm
  ),
  "\n"
)


# ================================================================
# 11. PROTEST
#
# Community distance vs. combined standardized environmental
# distance.
#
# Uses the same House-restricted, linked-Position permutation
# matrix.
# ================================================================

protest_bray.metric_houseperm <- vegan::protest(

  X =
    bray_dist.metric_houseperm,

  Y =
    env_dist.metric_houseperm,

  permutations =
    perm_env.metric_houseperm
)


protest_wunifrac.metric_houseperm <- vegan::protest(

  X =
    wunifrac_dist.metric_houseperm,

  Y =
    env_dist.metric_houseperm,

  permutations =
    perm_env.metric_houseperm
)


protest_uunifrac.metric_houseperm <- vegan::protest(

  X =
    uunifrac_dist.metric_houseperm,

  Y =
    env_dist.metric_houseperm,

  permutations =
    perm_env.metric_houseperm
)


get_protest.metric_houseperm <- function(
  obj_houseperm,
  metric_houseperm
) {

  data.frame(

    Metric =
      metric_houseperm,

    Procrustes_r =
      as.numeric(
        obj_houseperm$t0
      ),

    p_value =
      as.numeric(
        obj_houseperm$signif
      ),

    stringsAsFactors =
      FALSE
  )
}


protest_summary.metric_houseperm <- dplyr::bind_rows(

  get_protest.metric_houseperm(
    protest_bray.metric_houseperm,
    "Bray-Curtis"
  ),

  get_protest.metric_houseperm(
    protest_wunifrac.metric_houseperm,
    "Weighted UniFrac"
  ),

  get_protest.metric_houseperm(
    protest_uunifrac.metric_houseperm,
    "Unweighted UniFrac"
  )
)


cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "PROTEST SUMMARY\n",
  "HOUSE-RESTRICTED PERMUTATIONS\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)


print(
  protest_summary.metric_houseperm %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Procrustes_r =
        round(
          Procrustes_r,
          3
        ),
      p_value =
        signif(
          p_value,
          4
        )
    )
)


# ================================================================
# 12. Mantel tests
#
# One environmental variable at a time.
#
# These remain singleton environmental comparisons, but the
# permutation test now respects House and recurring Position.
# ================================================================

per_var_mantel.metric_houseperm <- function(
  comm_dist_houseperm,
  env_std_houseperm,
  env_vars_houseperm,
  permutation_matrix_houseperm
) {

  out_houseperm <- lapply(

    env_vars_houseperm,

    function(
      variable_houseperm
    ) {

      env_single_houseperm <- env_std_houseperm[
        ,
        variable_houseperm,
        drop = FALSE
      ]


      env_single_dist_houseperm <- stats::dist(
        env_single_houseperm,
        method = "euclidean"
      )


      fit_houseperm <- vegan::mantel(

        comm_dist_houseperm,

        env_single_dist_houseperm,

        method =
          "spearman",

        permutations =
          permutation_matrix_houseperm
      )


      data.frame(

        Variable =
          variable_houseperm,

        Effect =
          as.numeric(
            fit_houseperm$statistic
          ),

        p_value =
          as.numeric(
            fit_houseperm$signif
          ),

        stringsAsFactors =
          FALSE
      )
    }
  )


  do.call(
    rbind,
    out_houseperm
  )
}


bioenv_single_bray.metric_houseperm <-
  per_var_mantel.metric_houseperm(

    bray_dist.metric_houseperm,

    env_std.metric_houseperm,

    env_vars.metric_houseperm,

    perm_env.metric_houseperm
  )


bioenv_single_wunifrac.metric_houseperm <-
  per_var_mantel.metric_houseperm(

    wunifrac_dist.metric_houseperm,

    env_std.metric_houseperm,

    env_vars.metric_houseperm,

    perm_env.metric_houseperm
  )


bioenv_single_uunifrac.metric_houseperm <-
  per_var_mantel.metric_houseperm(

    uunifrac_dist.metric_houseperm,

    env_std.metric_houseperm,

    env_vars.metric_houseperm,

    perm_env.metric_houseperm
  )


bioenv_long.metric_houseperm <- dplyr::bind_rows(

  dplyr::mutate(
    bioenv_single_bray.metric_houseperm,
    Metric = "Bray-Curtis"
  ),

  dplyr::mutate(
    bioenv_single_wunifrac.metric_houseperm,
    Metric = "Weighted UniFrac"
  ),

  dplyr::mutate(
    bioenv_single_uunifrac.metric_houseperm,
    Metric = "Unweighted UniFrac"
  )
) %>%

  dplyr::mutate(

    Analysis =
      "BIO-ENV (singleton)",

    Stat =
      "Spearman r"
  )


cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "MANTEL RESULTS\n",
  "HOUSE-RESTRICTED PERMUTATIONS\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)


print(
  bioenv_long.metric_houseperm %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Effect =
        round(
          Effect,
          3
        ),
      p_value =
        signif(
          p_value,
          4
        )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      Metric,
      Variable
    ),
  n = Inf
)


# ================================================================
# 13. db-RDA
#
# ORIGINAL MODEL STRUCTURE RETAINED:
#
# For each environmental variable:
#
#   distance ~ focal_environmental_variable +
#              Condition(
#                House +
#                Growout +
#                Treatment +
#                Position
#              )
#
# Each physicochemical variable is therefore tested separately
# after accounting for the primary experimental factors.
#
# Other physicochemical variables are NOT included in Condition().
#
# Significance is tested with the revised House-restricted,
# linked-Position permutation matrix.
# ================================================================

per_var_dbrda.metric_houseperm <- function(

  comm_dist_houseperm,

  metric_label_houseperm,

  dat_houseperm,

  env_vars_houseperm,

  permutation_matrix_houseperm
) {

  results_houseperm <- lapply(

    env_vars_houseperm,

    function(
      variable_houseperm
    ) {

      formula_text_houseperm <- paste0(

        "comm_dist_houseperm ~ ",

        variable_houseperm,

        " + Condition(House + Growout + Treatment + Position)"
      )


      formula_houseperm <- stats::as.formula(
        formula_text_houseperm
      )


      model_houseperm <- vegan::dbrda(

        formula_houseperm,

        data =
          dat_houseperm
      )


      anova_houseperm <- vegan::anova.cca(

        model_houseperm,

        permutations =
          permutation_matrix_houseperm,

        model =
          "reduced"
      )


      pcol_houseperm <- grep(
        "^Pr\\(>F\\)$",
        colnames(
          anova_houseperm
        ),
        value = TRUE
      )


      if (
        length(
          pcol_houseperm
        ) == 1
      ) {

        p_houseperm <- as.numeric(
          anova_houseperm[
            1,
            pcol_houseperm,
            drop = TRUE
          ]
        )

      } else {

        p_houseperm <- NA_real_
      }


      r2_object_houseperm <- vegan::RsquareAdj(
        model_houseperm
      )


      adj_r2_houseperm <- as.numeric(
        r2_object_houseperm$adj.r.squared
      )


      data.frame(

        Variable =
          variable_houseperm,

        Effect =
          max(
            0,
            adj_r2_houseperm
          ),

        p_value =
          p_houseperm,

        Metric =
          metric_label_houseperm,

        Analysis =
          "db-RDA (partial)",

        Stat =
          "partial adj. R2",

        stringsAsFactors =
          FALSE
      )
    }
  )


  do.call(
    rbind,
    results_houseperm
  )
}


dbrda_bray_long.metric_houseperm <-
  per_var_dbrda.metric_houseperm(

    bray_dist.metric_houseperm,

    "Bray-Curtis",

    sample_data_df.metric_houseperm,

    env_vars.metric_houseperm,

    perm_env.metric_houseperm
  )


dbrda_wunifrac_long.metric_houseperm <-
  per_var_dbrda.metric_houseperm(

    wunifrac_dist.metric_houseperm,

    "Weighted UniFrac",

    sample_data_df.metric_houseperm,

    env_vars.metric_houseperm,

    perm_env.metric_houseperm
  )


dbrda_uunifrac_long.metric_houseperm <-
  per_var_dbrda.metric_houseperm(

    uunifrac_dist.metric_houseperm,

    "Unweighted UniFrac",

    sample_data_df.metric_houseperm,

    env_vars.metric_houseperm,

    perm_env.metric_houseperm
  )


dbrda_long.metric_houseperm <- dplyr::bind_rows(

  dbrda_bray_long.metric_houseperm,

  dbrda_wunifrac_long.metric_houseperm,

  dbrda_uunifrac_long.metric_houseperm
)


cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "db-RDA RESULTS\n",
  "HOUSE-RESTRICTED PERMUTATIONS\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)


print(
  dbrda_long.metric_houseperm %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Effect =
        round(
          Effect,
          4
        ),
      p_value =
        signif(
          p_value,
          4
        )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      Metric,
      Variable
    ),
  n = Inf
)


# ================================================================
# 14. Combine per-variable results across methods
#
# Maintains the same general structure used by the previous
# lollipop-plot workflow.
# ==============================================================

all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm <- dplyr::bind_rows(

  bioenv_long.metric_houseperm[
    ,
    c(
      "Variable",
      "Effect",
      "p_value",
      "Metric",
      "Analysis",
      "Stat"
    ),
    drop = FALSE
  ],

  perm_env_long.metric_houseperm[
    ,
    c(
      "Variable",
      "Effect",
      "p_value",
      "Metric",
      "Analysis",
      "Stat"
    ),
    drop = FALSE
  ],

  dbrda_long.metric_houseperm[
    ,
    c(
      "Variable",
      "Effect",
      "p_value",
      "Metric",
      "Analysis",
      "Stat"
    ),
    drop = FALSE
  ]
)


# ================================================================
# 15. Order variables, methods, and distance metrics
# ==============================================================

all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm$Variable <- factor(

  all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm$Variable,

  levels =
    env_vars.metric_houseperm
)


all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm$Analysis <- factor(

  all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm$Analysis,

  levels = c(
    "BIO-ENV (singleton)",
    "PERMANOVA (margin)",
    "db-RDA (partial)"
  )
)


all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm$Metric <- factor(

  all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm$Metric,

  levels = c(
    "Bray-Curtis",
    "Weighted UniFrac",
    "Unweighted UniFrac"
  )
)


# ================================================================
# 16. Significance stars
#
# Raw permutation p-values, matching the prior visualization.
# ==============================================================

all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm$stars <- dplyr::case_when(

  is.finite(
    all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm$p_value
  ) &
    all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm$p_value < 0.001 ~
    "***",

  is.finite(
    all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm$p_value
  ) &
    all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm$p_value < 0.01 ~
    "**",

  is.finite(
    all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm$p_value
  ) &
    all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm$p_value < 0.05 ~
    "*",

  TRUE ~
    ""
)


# ================================================================
# 17. Final combined table
# ==============================================================

cat(
  "\n============================================================\n",
  "FINAL PER-VARIABLE COMPARISON\n",
  "HOUSE-RESTRICTED PERMUTATIONS\n",
  "============================================================\n",
  sep = ""
)


print(

  all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm %>%

    dplyr::mutate(

      Effect =
        round(
          Effect,
          3
        ),

      p_value =
        signif(
          p_value,
          4
        )
    ) %>%

    dplyr::arrange(
      Analysis,
      Metric,
      Variable
    ),

  n = Inf
)

```

```{r}
# ================================================================
# LOLLIPOP PLOT — UPDATED HOUSE-RESTRICTED RESULTS
#
# Uses:
#   all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm
#
# Displays:
#   - Mantel: Spearman r
#   - PERMANOVA: partial R²
#   - db-RDA: partial adjusted R²
#
# Significance:
#   - filled point = p < 0.05
#   - open point   = p >= 0.05
#
# Aesthetics retained from previous finalized plot.
# Does NOT overwrite previous plot/data objects.
# ================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)


# ================================================================
# 1. Prepare plotting dataframe
# ================================================================

viz_df.metric_houseperm <- all_long_p_only.metric_houseperm %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Analysis = dplyr::recode(
      as.character(Analysis),
      "BIO-ENV (singleton)" = "Mantel",
      "PERMANOVA (margin)"  = "PERMANOVA",
      "db-RDA (partial)"    = "db-RDA"
    ),

    Variable = dplyr::recode(
      as.character(Variable),
      "Potassium.dry"   = "K",
      "Phosphorus.dry"  = "P",
      "Ammonium.N.dry"  = "NH4+",
      "Nitrogen.dry"    = "Total N"
    ),

    Variable = factor(
      Variable,
      levels = c(
        "Total N",
        "NH4+",
        "P",
        "K",
        "Moisture"
      )
    ),

    Metric = factor(
      as.character(Metric),
      levels = c(
        "Bray-Curtis",
        "Weighted UniFrac",
        "Unweighted UniFrac"
      )
    ),

    Significance = factor(
      dplyr::if_else(
        is.finite(p_value) & p_value < 0.05,
        "<0.05",
        "≥0.05"
      ),
      levels = c(
        "<0.05",
        "≥0.05"
      )
    )
  )


# ================================================================
# 2. Retain previous analysis colors
# ================================================================

analysis_cols.metric_houseperm <- c(
  "Mantel"    = "#2A788EFF",
  "PERMANOVA" = "#d3436e",
  "db-RDA"    = "#000004"
)


# ================================================================
# 3. Create facet labels with statistic used by each analysis
# ================================================================

viz_df.metric_houseperm <- viz_df.metric_houseperm %>%
  dplyr::mutate(

    Method = dplyr::case_when(
      Analysis == "Mantel"    ~ "Spearman r",
      Analysis == "PERMANOVA" ~ "partial R²",
      Analysis == "db-RDA"    ~ "partial adj. R²",
      TRUE                    ~ as.character(Stat)
    ),

    FacetLabel = paste0(
      Analysis,
      " (",
      Method,
      ")"
    )
  )


facet_levels.metric_houseperm <- c(
  "Mantel (Spearman r)",
  "PERMANOVA (partial R²)",
  "db-RDA (partial adj. R²)"
)


viz_df.metric_houseperm$FacetLabel <- factor(
  viz_df.metric_houseperm$FacetLabel,
  levels = facet_levels.metric_houseperm
)


# ================================================================
# 4. Lollipop plot
# ================================================================

p_methods_lollipop.metric_houseperm <- ggplot(
  viz_df.metric_houseperm,
  aes(
    y = Variable,
    x = Effect
  )
) +

  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "black"
  ) +

  geom_segment(
    aes(
      x = 0,
      xend = Effect,
      yend = Variable,
      color = Analysis
    ),
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +

  # Base white point
  geom_point(
    shape = 21,
    size = 3.6,
    stroke = 0,
    fill = "white"
  ) +

  # Colored outline
  geom_point(
    aes(
      color = Analysis
    ),
    shape = 21,
    size = 3.6,
    stroke = 1.0,
    fill = NA
  ) +

  # Colored fill for statistically significant results
  geom_point(
    aes(
      fill = Analysis,
      alpha = Significance
    ),
    shape = 21,
    size = 3.6,
    stroke = 0
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = analysis_cols.metric_houseperm,
    guide = "none"
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = analysis_cols.metric_houseperm,
    guide = "none"
  ) +

  scale_alpha_manual(
    values = c(
      "<0.05" = 1,
      "≥0.05" = 0
    ),
    limits = c(
      "<0.05",
      "≥0.05"
    ),
    drop = FALSE,
    name = "Significance"
  ) +

  facet_grid(
    Metric ~ FacetLabel,
    scales = "free"
  ) +

  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +

  theme_bw(
    base_size = 11
  ) +

  theme(
    legend.position  = "top",
    legend.title     = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      color = "black"
    ),
    legend.text      = element_text(
      color = "black"
    ),
    axis.text.x      = element_text(
      color = "black"
    ),
    axis.text.y      = element_text(
      color = "black"
    ),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text.x     = element_text(
      size = 12,
      color = "black"
    ),
    strip.text.y     = element_text(
      color = "black"
    )
  ) +

  guides(
    alpha = guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(
        shape  = 21,
        size   = 5,
        stroke = 1.0,
        color  = "black",
        fill   = c(
          "<0.05" = "black",
          "≥0.05" = "white"
        ),
        alpha  = 1
      )
    )
  )


# ================================================================
# 5. Display
# ================================================================

print(
  p_methods_lollipop.metric_houseperm
)


# ================================================================
# 6. Export
# ================================================================

ggsave(
  "nutrient.lollipop.metric.houseperm.png",
  p_methods_lollipop.metric_houseperm,
  width = 7.5,
  height = 5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 900
)
```
